questions.q: Choose the best meaning: 'Patience is the key to relief.'
choices: Wait calmly and things will improve
questions.fact: Omani elders repeat this proverb at hard times.

questions.q: Complete the proverb: 'The falaj feeds ___ the palms.'
questions.fact: Shared water taught Omanis fairness for centuries.

questions.q: 'A guest is a gift.' In Oman this means:
questions.fact: Coffee and dates greet every guest in Oman.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the idiom correctly?
choices: The news spread like wildfire through the souq.
questions.fact: Souq gossip truly travels faster than wind.

questions.q: 'Still waters run deep' is closest to:
questions.fact: Falaj water runs silent but strong underground.

questions.q: Choose the polite request:
choices: Could you show me the way to the fort, please?
questions.fact: Politeness opens every door in the souq.

questions.q: What does 'to weather the storm' mean?
questions.fact: Dhow captains weathered monsoons for centuries.

questions.q: 'Many hands make light work' matches which Omani tradition?
questions.fact: Whole villages once pulled dhows to the sea.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported speech: 'I saw a whale,' said Salim.
choices: Salim said he had seen a whale.
Salim said he sees a whale.
questions.fact: Whale tales grow bigger every time they are told.

questions.q: 'Don't count your chickens before they hatch' means:
choices: Don't assume success before it happens
questions.fact: Fishermen say: don't sell the fish before the net lands.

questions.q: Passage: 'The aflaj are not merely channels; they are contracts written in water between generations.' The author suggests aflaj are:
choices: a social inheritance as much as engineering
questions.fact: Five Omani aflaj are UNESCO World Heritage sites.

questions.q: Passage: 'Bahla wears its legends lightly; ask a potter about the jinn and he smiles into his clay.' The potter's smile suggests:
choices: fond, playful familiarity with the tales
he does not know the legends
questions.fact: Bahla's jinn tales are told with a wink, not fear.

questions.q: Which is the best summary? 'Khareef transforms Dhofar: mist drapes the mountains, waterfalls awaken, and the land, for three months, forgets it was ever dry.'
choices: The monsoon briefly turns Dhofar lush and green
questions.fact: Khareef runs roughly June to September in Salalah.

questions.q: 'The dhow was stitched like a garment, its planks sewn with coir rope.' 'Stitched' is used:
questions.fact: Sewn boats flex with the waves instead of breaking.

questions.q: What is the tone? 'Beware Umm al-Duwais, they whispered, beauty with golden anklets — yet the tale, told to children, guards more morals than doors.'
questions.fact: Cautionary tales taught children wisdom, not fear.

questions.q: 'The lighthouse does not guide; it promises.' This line means:
choices: its light is a pledge of safe return
questions.fact: Families watched for their fathers' sails for months.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct subjunctive:
choices: The elder insisted that the water turn be respected.
The elder insisted the water turn was respected be.
The elder insisted the water to be respected.
The elder insisted be the water respected.
questions.fact: Falaj turns are still respected in mountain villages.

questions.q: 'Rosewater is the mountain's signature.' This is an example of:
questions.fact: Jebel Akhdar rosewater signs every Omani celebration.

questions.q: Which option best paraphrases: 'Trade winds wrote Oman's history long before historians did.'
choices: Oman's past was shaped by sea trade early on
questions.fact: Omani merchants reached China in the 9th century.

questions.q: 'Her voice carried the weight of untold tales' — 'weight' here suggests:
questions.fact: Grandmothers are the libraries of Omani folklore.
